key_insight: A small, clinically meaningful set of readily available patient features can make zero-shot LLMs more effective for CKD screening than using the full feature set.
clinical_relevance: This could help community and resource-limited settings screen for chronic kidney disease earlier without requiring dataset-specific model training or extensive laboratory inputs.
method: Selected a compact feature subset using ML-based feature analysis.
Serialized tabular patient records into standardized text prompts for zero-shot inference.
Compared four LLMs across three heterogeneous CKD datasets from three countries using full vs selected features.
evidence_signal: Across models and datasets, the selected feature set produced consistent, statistically significant gains in balanced accuracy and probability estimates, with performance described as suitable for screening.
watch_item: The approach still needs careful external validation and deployment testing because LLM performance can shift with population differences, prompt design, and real-world data quality.
paper_title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models
